fields.h1: Build a Testimonial Form That Gets Quotes Cleared to Publish
fields.hero_description: Build a testimonial form that records consent, sends edited quotes for approval, and saves each one to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Happens Between Submit and Publish
fields.features_subheading: A quote is usable once the client has agreed to its wording and to the name beside it. The form gets both answers in writing.
fields.feature_1:
Permission asked in its own question

A checkbox asks whether the quote may be published, and the next question asks how the name should read: full name, first name and initial, initials only, or no name at all.
fields.feature_2:
Questions that pull out a before and after

The form asks what was going wrong before the work began and what changed once it ended. A quote built from both answers reads like a short story, not a general line of praise.
fields.feature_3:
Edited wording goes back to the client

When you shorten a quote, the app emails the client the new wording with an Approve button. The quote's status changes to Client approved only after that click is recorded.
fields.feature_4:
A headshot or logo filed with each quote

Clients can attach a headshot or a company logo beside their answers. Each file is saved with its quote, so the face or logo on your site belongs to the person you are quoting.
fields.feature_5:
Every testimonial is a searchable row

Each testimonial lands as a row in a database you own, tagged with the service, the date, and the display name. Sales can search it for a quote about the exact service a buyer wants.
fields.feature_6:
Your form's code, yours to keep

On paid plans, export the full code of the form and its database to your GitHub repository. A developer can then show the approved quotes on your own site or add new fields.

fields.tab_content_1:
Before any quote runs, the client approves it

Quarry Lane Design sends the form when a website project closes. Ruth Abernathy of Kettle Hill Florist writes a long answer, and the studio cuts it to one claim: 40 online orders in its first week. The app emails Ruth that wording with an Approve button, and the status reads Client approved after she clicks.
fields.tab_content_2:
On the site he is Marek D., the name he picked

Wren Bastian Coaching sends the form at the end of its 12-week program. Marek Dobrowski writes that he booked 11 discovery calls in 12 weeks. Asked how his name should appear, he picks first name and last initial, so the site runs his quote as Marek D. That choice is saved in the same row as the quote.
fields.tab_content_3:
Oak Hollow quotes on hand when a listing comes up

Celeste Navarro of Bayline Realty sends sellers the form on closing day, and each quote is tagged with its neighborhood. When an Oak Hollow owner asks her to list a house, she filters by Oak Hollow and finds 4 quotes from past sellers. The Lindqvists, who sold in 9 days, lead her listing presentation.

A $10 thank-you, noted under every quote

Driftwood Roasting Co. gives a $10 store credit to every customer who sends a testimonial, at any rating. Tobias Ferreira rates the Night Shift blend 4 stars and gets the credit by email. On the product page, his quote carries the line Received a $10 store credit, because the credit is saved with his answers.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Testimonial Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan the questions, consent and approval for a testimonial form, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide where the quotes will run
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the places a quote will appear, such as the homepage or a sales deck. Where it runs decides what you ask. A quote for a pricing page needs a result with a number in it, while a homepage quote can be one plain sentence.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open with the problem the client had before hiring you, then ask what changed. Add one question for a number they can stand behind, such as hours saved or calls booked. Keep the form short enough to finish in a few minutes.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for consent after the answers, when the client can see what they wrote. Use a checkbox for permission to publish and a separate choice for how the name appears. Getting both in writing gives you a record to point to later.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write a prompt that lists your questions, the consent checkbox, and the name choices. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it. Change any part by prompting again, for example to add a photo upload for headshots or company logos.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide who edits quotes and how the client signs off on the edit. Ask for a status field on each quote and an email that sends the client the edited text. The status should change to approved only when the client confirms it.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Add tags the answers fill in, like the service bought or the client's industry. When a prospect asks about one service, you can filter for quotes about exactly that service instead of scrolling through every testimonial you have.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send it the week the result shows
fields.howto_step_7_des: Send the link right after the client sees the result, while the details are fresh. Before that, submit a test answer yourself and confirm the row saved with its tags, its consent choice, and the display name.

faq_plan.a: A testimonial form is a short online form that asks a client or customer to describe their experience in their own words. The business then quotes them on its website or in sales material. A good one also records whether the quote may run and under what name.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a testimonial form?
faq_plan.a: Write a prompt that says who fills it in and where the quotes will be published. Emergent's AI form builder turns that into the form and a database for the answers, and you can change either one by prompting again. Fill it in once yourself before you send the link to a client.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a testimonial form template include?
faq_plan.a: Start with five: the problem before, what changed, a number that shows the change, permission to publish, and how the name should appear. A testimonial form PDF can ask the same things, but someone has to copy each answer out of the file, while an online form saves every answer as a row.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a free testimonial form for my small business?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing. If you work with clients over weeks, send an assessment form when the work starts, too: the baseline it records gives the testimonial at the end a before number to compare against.

faq_plan.q: How does a testimonial form ask permission to publish a quote?
faq_plan.a: With a question of its own, apart from the rating. A checkbox names where the quote may appear, and a second choice sets the display name. The FTC's guidance says a business can feature customers' comments in its ads, but if they had a reason to expect a benefit, the ad should disclose that. It adds that even the chance to be featured might be seen as having a value.

faq_plan.q: When is the right time to send a testimonial form?
faq_plan.a: Send it in the week the client sees the result they paid for: launch week for a website, closing day for a home sale. If no answer comes back within a week, send one reminder with the link. Ask Emergent to add an email reminder that goes out on the schedule you set.

faq_plan.q: Can a testimonial form also collect suggestions for improvement?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as long as the suggestions sit in a separate question that is never published. You can also send criticism to a feedback form of its own, where it reaches the person who can fix the problem and the testimonial table holds only quotes you may run.

faq_plan.q: Can testimonial forms collect photos and video?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add an upload field for a headshot, a company logo or a short video clip, and each file is saved with the answers it belongs to. Cover the image in the same consent question as the quote. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps.

faq_plan.q: Can I offer a reward for filling out a testimonial form?
faq_plan.a: You can, if the reward depends on sending the form, not on what the person writes. The FTC's final rule prohibits businesses from providing compensation or other incentives conditioned on the writing of consumer reviews expressing a particular sentiment, either positive or negative. Offer the same thank-you at any rating, and note it beside the quote when you publish it.

faq_plan.q: Can I use a testimonial form for employee testimonials?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Swap the client questions for ones about the job: what the role is like day to day and what made them stay. Keep the permission checkbox and the name choice: each person decides how their quote appears on the careers page. For a lighter staff spotlight, pair it with a favorite things questionnaire.

findings.quote: The FTC's guidance for advertisers says a business can ask customers about their experiences and feature their comments in its ads, and the checkbox keeps a written record of each yes.
findings.issue: Source scope dropped (rework-checklist 2). The quoted FTC answer (Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking, the question about quoting customers in ads) continues: 'if you've given these customers a reason to expect a benefit from providing their thoughts about your product, you should disclose that fact in your ads', and says even being told in advance they might be featured can be such a benefit ('Customers were told in advance they might be featured in an ad.'). The page states only the permissive half and pairs it with the consent checkbox, implying a recorded yes is what the FTC asks for. The source does not say the unconditional version. Only instance of this class on the page; the FAQ 9 FTC sentence stays inside its span.
findings.fix: Either keep the FTC's condition in the sentence and add the span to domain_sources (e.g. 'The FTC's guidance says a business can feature customers' comments in its ads, and that if they expected a benefit, or knew in advance they might be featured, the ad should say so.'), or cut the FTC sentence and let the checkbox stand as advice ('the checkbox keeps a written record of each yes').
